title: Arcane Tower
html:

↑
Arcane Tower → Selûnite Outpost
The Arcane Tower is a Location within the Underdark in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3. The tower overlooks the Ebonlake, and belongs to  Lenore De Hurst. However, she has not returned home in over a decade.
“
New sounds through damp and dark oppression break.
Is it the foe, that foul, contemptuous heel?
„
— Bernard, asking the rhymed parole

Overview

Access

The Arcane Tower is in the south-west corner of the Underdark map. This area is recognizable by its neatly built stone entryway that opens to a front garden featuring two  Arcane Turrets. It can be reached through the Torchstalk Gulch, recognisable by its dark brown paths paved with deep red mushroom clusters and spots of Torchstalk that cast floating embers into the air.[1]

The area is divided roughly into the entry area, each floor of the tower, and the garden outside the ground floor. Upon initial approach, the doors are shut and the central elevator is disabled; the floors must be accessed through other means.

The party can use the fungus platforms growing around the tower to  Jump their way down to the ground floor, starting either from the southern balcony of the Second floor, or from the breach in stone railing near entrance at X: 3 Y: -296 (just behind the turret). It is a good idea to cast  Feather Fall to prevent unnecessary fall damage. Alternatively, using  Fly or teleporting (via  Misty Step) also gets the party down without issues.

Dealing with the Arcane Turrets

The Arcane Tower is guarded by automated  Arcane Turrets. They are automatically hostile and shoot at the party whenever they are in the line of sight and in range; there is a targeting indicator which can show this. Anything that breaks this line of sight (e.g. solid obstacles or  Fog Cloud) effectively stops the attacks.

The turrets shoot and attack in real-time exploration mode as well as in turn-based mode. However, it is recommended to turn on turn-based mode to make movement and controlling the party more manageable.

In general, there are a few approaches to dealing with these the Arcane Cannons:

  • Attacking - the cannons can be directly damaged and rendered inoperable. They have some resistances, and vulnerability to ⁠Lightning.
  • Override - the cannons can be shut down once restoring power on the generator on the ground floor.
  • Running by / Stealth - this is best done in turn-based mode as it allows the party members to move cover-to-cover between turns.
  • Anti-Magic - as the Arcane Cannons are magical constructs, they can be shut down by placing a  Sussur Bloom near them, because of their  Sussur Antimagic Field.
    • Sussur Blooms can be found in the garden at the bottom of the Arcane Tower, or at the Sussur Tree in Dread Hollow.
    • Attacking a Cannon while it is shut-down by the Anti-Magic field destroys it, as opposed to "knocking it out".
    • Cannons which have previously been rendered inoperable but not destroyed can actually be revived by the Sussur Antimagic Field, by first placing and then taking back a Sussur Bloom near them.

Ground floor (generator room)

The door to the Ground floor is locked (requires  DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick). However, it can also be opened with a lever from inside, and a Hole at X: -50 Y: -304 (detected with  DC 5 Perception Check) allows any small summon (like  Mage Hand) to seep inside and use the lever.

Once inside, the clues on how to restore power to the generator of the Arcane Tower are clear: several  Withered Blue Petals on the floor near its furnace, and also a book titled  Treatise on the Antimagic Properties of Sussur Tree Flowers on the workbench nearby.

A  Sussur Bloom must be inserted in the power generator. Sussur Blooms can be found at the Garden just outside the door, or taken from the giant sussur tree in the Dread Hollow.

The party must interact with the Power Generator to bring up the crafting menu and use it to combine the machine with a Sussur Bloom. The Arcane tower comes to life, granting 25 xp and the inspiration ⁠Regeneration for party members with the  Guild Artisan background. Once the generator is powered, the Arcane Turrets power down, the Arcane Braziers become lit, and the elevator can be used to ascend and descend between the floors.

At halfway from the generator room to the elevator chamber, at X: -53 Y: -284, in a Gilded Chest lies the  Uncovered Mysteries necklace. Also, the barrels and crates around the elevator and in the generator room contain a fair amount of alchemical ingredients, mostly of mushroom and crystal derivation.

First floor (greenhouse)

This floor can only be accessed by the restored elevator, by flying, or by using the platforms on the exterior fungus on the south side of the tower. This is a level that contains all the mushrooms required for the quest ⁠Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite.

The other notable item on this floor is the  Threadbare Book containing the phrase: "How can I trust? How should I know? How can I show myself, my darkest me?", which provides an additional option for interacting with  Bernard on the roof.

Second floor (main entrance)

The main floor can be accessed directly through the front door of the tower, or via the elevator after it is powered. Opening the Main Door requires succeeding on a  DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check, or it can be broken down - it has  Medium Toughness and 36 hit points. Alternatively, there is a broken window to the left of the door that can be entered. Opening this door prior to the restoration of power leads to a confrontation with two Arcane Turrets, one of which is stationed right across the broken window.

A Dusty Book can be found on this floor. After reading, it changes its title to  Evil's Ascent.

On the northern balcony is the  Chest of the Mundane, which is revealed as magical with a successful Arcana check. Taking the clutter from the chest in the inventory, or placing a Sussur Bloom near the chest, dispels the illusion to reveal some scrolls and  Mystra's Grace. The latter can provide the party an additional casting of  Feather Fall which can help them avoid some damage trying to access the ground floor. Observing the effects of the chest grants the inspirational event ⁠Trash & Treasure for characters with the  Guild Artisan.

The southern balcony does not contain any notable items, but lets the party access the exterior fungus platforms to the lower levels.

Third floor (bedroom)

This floor can only be accessed by the restored elevator or by flying. If wanting a peaceful interaction with Bernard, this floor contains documents the party can inspect prior to ascending to the fourth floor (roof).

The book  The Roads to Darkness can be found on the desk at the South-Eastern corner at X: -25 Y: -297 and a  Torn-Out Paper on the table close to the elevator at X: -35 Y: -286. The book contains a stance that leads Bernard to take the player character for the tower hostess, while the separate page provides them with an additional interaction with the automaton.

The  Orpheus, Prince of the Comet, Part One: Betrayal can be found on top of a bookshelf at X: -31 Y: -296. If  Lae'zel is in the party, she can read it straightaway; if she is not available, the disc can be read after picking up and using the  The Careful Art of Tir'su Ciphers from the table near the elevator at X: -32 Y: -292, or after succeeding on a  DC 20 Intelligence Check. Also, the player character may discuss the disc with Lae'zel upon returning to the camp. Either way, deciphering the disc starts a quest ⁠Discover the History of Prince Orpheus.

Aside from the books and notes, the magical ring  Mage's Friend can also be looted on this floor in a wooden chest by the bed, at X: -29 Y: -273.

Lastly, there is an interactable button at the north-eastern corner of the tower which appears to do nothing when pressed. To function, the party must retrieve and equip the  Dog Collar from the grave at the Dread Hollow at X: -41 Y: -212, prior to interacting with it. Doing so reveals the button served as a food dispenser for Lenore's pet, Myrna, as a piece of  Raw Steak appears, but only if the button is pressed by the same party member who wears the collar. If the collar had been dug up, but was not equipped, or the button was pressed by another character, the party member currently having it in the inventory or wearing it comments, feeling it vibrating. The button can be pressed multiple time, but gives the treat only once and after that its mechanism is deactivated.

The Handwritten Letter ( Letter from Amarith after the first reading) on Lenore's desk sheds some light on Myrna's story, and also on reasons that caused a  Bulette to roam around the tower. If Myrna's grave in the Dread Hollow has not been inspected by the party by this moment, reading the letter adds an option to place an  Autumncrocus on it, earning approval from  Gale,  Karlach and  Wyll.

The fourth floor (roof)

This floor can only be accessed by the restored elevator or by flying. Upon arriving at the floor, a dialogue is triggered with  Bernard, who is standing guard by the elevator along with a group of Animated Armours.

Bernard speaks only in poetry, with the scattered lines found throughout the Arcane Tower serving as various command phrases for him. In the first meeting, if the party read  The Roads to Darkness they can respond with "Or art though friend, a rescue from my lonely wake?" which prevents Bernard from becoming hostile and attacking. Of all character Classes, only  Bards can roll a passive  DC 18 History Check here, and if successful, they remember the correct line continuing the stanza. Successfully placating Bernard grants the party 50 XP, and also earns the ⁠Heart of the Creator inspirational event to any party member with  Entertainer.

Afterwards, there are several dialogue options / commands the party can use with Bernard, depending on what they have read (see #Bernard's commands).

The  Guiding Light ring can be obtained by reciting "How can I trust? How will I ever know? / How can I show myself, my darkest me?" from the  Threadbare Book on the first floor, or by destroying Bernard in combat. It cannot be pick-pocketed. Destroying Bernard (or commanding them to drop their weapon) also grants the party the  Light of Creation.

There is also a lever next to a bookshelf at X: -40 Y: -296, which can be noticed with a  DC 18 Perception Check. This is an alternate way to open the wall on the first floor that leads to the basement.

Lastly, there is the Stool of Hill Giant Strength at X: -26 Y: -272, behind one of the Animated Armours. Party members can sit on the stool and notice its magical effect, as well as its disappearance once they stand up. If they break the stool, they can obtain the  Club of Hill Giant Strength from its debris.

The basement (secret room)

There are several ways to access the basement:

  • Using the elevator with  Guiding Light equipped (an additional "Basement" button appears at the controls)
  • Using  Fly or  Misty Step to go through a gap from the first floor
  • Using  Mage Hand or a ranged attack to activate a lever under the staircase to open the wall
  • Activating the lever on the fourth floor hidden next to a bookshelf.

In the basement, aside from more  Tongue of Madness and  Timmask Spores, the party can also find the  Staff of Arcane Blessing leaning against a table,  The Sparkswall in a gilded chest, and an assortment of scrolls in the chest and various rows of books.

Layout

Arcane Tower layout
Level How to access Notable elements
Ground floor (Generator) The exterior Garden can be access by flight, jumping or teleporting on outside the tower. The locked ground floor itself can be accessed by the Back Door or through a Hole in the wall. Contains the generator that allows you to restore power to the tower. The elevator itself is located on a mezzanine, with the rest of the basement beneath it.
1st Floor (Greenhouse) Can be reached by the elevator, flight, or by jumping or teleporting on the mushrooms on the tower exterior. Contains the quest related items  Tongue of Madness,  Timmask Spores). If the party don't want to explore the rest of the tower, they only have to visit this one floor.
2nd Floor (Main Entrance) Can be accessed by the Main Door. Or flight and elevator if approaching from another level. Contains the Chest of Mundane with  Mystra's Grace + two Scrolls) and 2x Arcane Cannons.
3rd Floor (Bedroom) Can be reached by the elevator and / or flight. Contains key elements that allows the party to converse with Bernard and other constructs peacefully.
4th Floor (Roof) Can be reached by the elevator and / or flight. This level contains Bernard, and the  Guiding Light ring which is one method to visit the basement.
Basement (Secret Room) Can be reached by the elevator with the  Guiding Light ring equipped, by flying or using  Misty Step through a gap from the 1st level, by using  Mage Hand to activate a lever under the staircase, by using a bow to activate the lever under the staircase through the staircase, or by activating the lever on the 4th floor hidden next to a bookshelf. Contains treasures - including the  Staff of Arcane Blessing,  The Sparkswall, and another set of the quest items Tongue of Madness, Timmask Spores).

Bernard's commands

Line Action Required book
"How can I trust? How will I ever know? / How can I show myself, my darkest me?" Bernard gives  Guiding Light to the player character.  Threadbare Book (first floor / greenhouse)
"These empty sheets are all that's left of you. / The last of all the thoughtless gifts you gave." Bernard gives the player character a  Potion of Greater Healing.  Patched Parchment (table next to Bernard, fourth floor)
"The silence stretches on - I'm all alone. / Please, can I hold your hands, for just a while?" Bernard hugs the player character and reassure them. It speaks as if the player character is Lenore.  Torn-Out Paper (third floor / bedroom)
"Or art thou friend, a rescue from my lonely wake?" Bernard acknowledges the player character as their master, and remains passive.  The Roads to Darkness (third floor / bedroom)
"There is a light in every living thing. / It's crawling t'wards the surface to survive." Bernard and the nearby Animated Armours become hostile and attack.  Evil's Ascent (second floor / main entrance, marked as Dusty Book before reading it)

Related locations

Torchstalk Gulch

To the east of the tower, this unnamed area of the Underdark has deep red mushroom clusters and spots of Torchstalk that cast floating embers into the air. The corpse of an unfortunate Drow can be found, having been killed by an unexpected fall.

The party can climb mushrooms along the wall to reach an upper level. Some of these mushrooms are illusions that de-materialise when stepped on or discovered with a  DC 10 Investigation Check. There are also some mushroom circles, one behind an illusory wall, on the upper level and below. These connect to each other, until the circle in the Overgrown Tunnel is used. They can then be used to travel to the Overgrown Tunnel near the the Riverside Teahouse and back.

Festering Cove

Main article: The Festering Cove

The Festering Cove is a partially hidden location on a separate Underdark map, where  Kuo-toa worship their "god",  BOOOAL. It can be reached by climbing down the cragged rock in Torchstalk Gulch X: 80 Y: -241.

First floor

  • Broken Machineries

Third floor (bedroom)

  • Mage's Friend in a chest at the foot of the bed on the 3rd floor

Fourth floor (roof)

  • Broken Machineries
  • Club of Hill Giant Strength from breaking the Stool of Hill Giant Strength on the 4th floor of the tower
  • Guiding Light looted or gifted from Bernard after using the appropriate play line
  • Light of Creation looted from Bernard (can also use  Command: Drop)

Basement (secret room)

  • Staff of Arcane Blessing
  • The Sparkswall
  • Timmask Spores
  • Tongues of Madness
  • Level 3 Spell Scroll (randomised)

Alchemy

Apart from  Timmask Spores and  Tongue of Madness, the latter of which can be looted only in the Arcane Tower, this location is the only place where the player character can obtain  Broken Machinery (on the fourth floor and also in crates on the second floor) used to craft  Elixir of Lightning Resistance.
